input.rationale: We hold a convenience termination right on one month's notice (better than our preferred 30 days), IBM must continue performing through the final termination date, and IBM has no convenience right at all — only termination for uncured material breach under § 3.3. Noted, not flagged here: the early termination charges referenced in Attachment A are unquantified; we address capping them under the LD rule to avoid duplicating the same commercial ask.

input.quote: Type I Materials are those, created during the Service performance period, in which Customer will have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright).
input.rationale: We own Type I Materials created for us, IBM retains its pre-existing Type II Materials but grants us an irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up licence, and there is no assignment of our Content or data to IBM and no joint ownership — this meets the fallback. Noted, not flagged: the Type II licence is limited to use within our US Enterprise with no modify/sublicense right, Materials default to Type II if unspecified, the licence-back to IBM over Type I Materials permits external distribution and derivative works, and there is no affirmative statement that we retain ownership of Content — points we would negotiate as secondary asks.

input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Base Components licence is expressly revocable, is limited to us alone (no Affiliates or contractors, with § 14.17 confirming no other rights are granted, unlike the Type II Materials licence which covers our Enterprise) and offers no path to add them — squarely our walk-away case. Redline deletes "revocable", ties termination of the licence to Section 3, and extends it to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: There is no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against us and no right of access to our systems or premises; § 11.3 is only an acceptable-use investigation right, exercisable on reasonable-efforts prior notice before restricting access or removing Content. The absence of Customer-facing audit rights matches our preferred position, so nothing to redline.
